open_points.subject: OwnerSession monotonic deadlines
open_points.text: Every duration in this decision ... is measured by the process's monotonic clock ...; instants Registry records ... are UTC wall-clock time. M11 lists only the UTC began, expiry and last-request instants among the session's facts.
open_points.question: What monotonic-clock facts or deadlines does an OwnerSession retain so that its limits can be enforced without deriving them from wall-clock instants?
options: Keep separate monotonic began, last-request and deadline values as runtime facts
Keep only monotonic deadlines and retain the UTC instants for display or records
Derive deadlines from the UTC instants despite wall-clock changes
open_points.default_guess: Keep separate monotonic began and last-request values, derive both monotonic deadlines from them, and treat the UTC instants as informational facts only.

open_points.subject: Meaning of the process's monotonic clock
open_points.text: measured by the process's monotonic clock, which a change of the wall clock does not move
open_points.question: Does elapsed session, confirmation and lockout time include time while the host or VM is suspended?
options: Use a monotonic clock that excludes suspend time
Use a boot-time monotonic clock that includes suspend time
open_points.default_guess: Use the platform's ordinary monotonic clock, excluding suspended time.

open_points.subject: Periodic session-ending pass
open_points.text: a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the start
open_points.question: When is the first pass, and how are later passes scheduled when a pass lasts beyond its nominal interval?
options: First pass 60 seconds after start, fixed-rate and non-overlapping, skipping missed ticks
First pass immediately at start, then fixed-rate
Wait 60 seconds after each pass finishes
Run catch-up passes for missed ticks
open_points.default_guess: Run the first pass 60 seconds after start and then on a fixed-rate, non-overlapping schedule, skipping ticks missed while a pass is still running.

open_points.subject: Locks held by the session-ending pass
open_points.text: taking the import lock and then each session's lock ... and deciding under them
open_points.question: Does one pass hold the import lock while it visits all sessions, or release and reacquire it separately for each session?
options: Hold the import lock for the entire pass and take each session lock beneath it
Acquire and release the import lock together with each individual session lock
open_points.default_guess: Hold the import lock for the entire pass so the set of uploaded files cannot change while expired sessions are removed.

open_points.subject: Admitted owner request racing expiry cleanup or sign-out
open_points.text: a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs ... requests ... take the import lock before [the session lock] ... the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import lock and then each session's lock
open_points.question: What happens when a request passes the session check, then waits for the locks, and a sign-out or expiry pass acquires those locks first and removes the session or its uploaded file?
options: Admission pins the session and its file until the request finishes
Lock acquisition rechecks the session and refuses the request
The request proceeds with a detached snapshot of the session state
Ordering is determined at lock acquisition rather than at the earlier session check
open_points.default_guess: Admission pins the session state needed by the request; cleanup may mark it ended but cannot remove that state until every already-admitted request finishes.

open_points.subject: Import-lock release point
open_points.question: At what exact point is an upload, mapping, confirmation, import or sign-out request 'done' for releasing the import and session locks?
options: After all validation and state changes are committed and the response data is materialized
After response rendering completes
After the response has been fully transmitted to the browser
open_points.default_guess: Release the locks after validation and commit and after taking an immutable response snapshot, before transmitting the response.

open_points.subject: Configuration variable names
open_points.text: The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_ ... It holds exactly these items and no other
open_points.question: What is the exact environment-variable name for each store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential and service token?
options: Declare one fixed REGISTRY_ name for each item
Derive token variable names from service names by an unstated naming rule
open_points.default_guess: Declare fixed uppercase names such as REGISTRY_STORE, REGISTRY_BACKUP_LOCATION, REGISTRY_BACKUP_KEY, REGISTRY_OWNER_CREDENTIAL and one explicitly named token variable per service.

open_points.subject: Configuration well-formedness
open_points.text: each well formed; each secret's length ... A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start
open_points.question: What exact syntax, encoding and allowed value set makes each configuration item well formed, including how environment text is converted to the byte length used for secrets?
options: Secrets are UTF-8 text and length is the encoded byte length; locations must be absolute filesystem paths
Secrets use a declared binary encoding such as base64 or hexadecimal; locations must be absolute paths
Accept relative paths and arbitrary environment text using the platform's native encoding
open_points.default_guess: Require absolute filesystem paths and base64-encoded secret bytes, measuring the decoded byte length.

open_points.subject: Relative configured paths
open_points.text: compared by their absolute paths with every symbolic link resolved
open_points.question: Are relative store or backup paths refused, or, if accepted, relative to which stable directory are they made absolute?
options: Refuse every relative path
Resolve relative paths against the process working directory
Resolve them against a release- or configuration-defined directory

open_points.subject: New-store temporary suffix
open_points.text: under a temporary name — the store's name with a suffix the release declares
open_points.question: What exact suffix does the release declare, and what collision rule applies if the real store name itself already ends with that suffix?
options: Declare one fixed suffix and treat it purely as an appended literal
Generate a per-start random suffix
Reserve a separate fixed temporary filename
open_points.default_guess: Use one fixed reserved appended suffix and remove only that exact sibling path before creating a new store.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption and container format
open_points.text: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key ... it records, readable without its key, its instant, the release, the last audit sequence number ... and a digest of the key
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce construction, key interpretation, metadata encoding and key-digest algorithm define a valid backup and detect ciphertext or header tampering?
options: Define a versioned authenticated-encryption container with authenticated cleartext metadata
Encrypt the SQLite bytes without authenticating the cleartext record
Rely on the later SQLite integrity check for integrity
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD container with a random nonce, authenticate all cleartext metadata as associated data, interpret the configured key as fixed-length decoded bytes, and use a declared cryptographic key identifier rather than an ad hoc digest.

open_points.subject: Backup filename namespaces
open_points.text: Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release declares ... A kept name is made from the backup's instant
open_points.question: What are the exact prefixes and the exact collision-free encoding of an instant into a kept filename?
options: Fixed prefixes plus a UTC timestamp with declared subsecond precision
Fixed prefixes plus a timestamp and random suffix
Fixed prefixes plus a timestamp and content digest
open_points.default_guess: Declare fixed reserved prefixes and use a canonical UTC timestamp with sufficient subsecond precision plus a random suffix, while never overwriting an existing name.

open_points.subject: Backup clock polling
open_points.text: The process looks at the clock at least once a minute; a date's run starts at its first look at or after 03:00
open_points.question: What polling cadence and phase must implementations use, especially around starts, scheduler delays and wall-clock jumps?
options: Poll on each UTC minute boundary
Poll every fixed 60 monotonic seconds from process start
Permit any cadence no slower than once per minute
open_points.default_guess: Poll on UTC minute boundaries and record each observation used by the crossing rule.

open_points.subject: Integrity of already-kept backups
open_points.text: Registry decrypts a backup only to check it when it is made ... every kept backup is encrypted, consistent, checked
open_points.question: Is consistency guaranteed only when a backup is first kept, or must later runs revalidate existing kept backups so corruption after creation cannot leave an inconsistent file counted and shown as a kept backup?
options: Guarantee only that each backup passed when created
Revalidate every kept backup during every run
Periodically revalidate kept backups on a separate schedule
open_points.default_guess: State the guarantee as 'passed when created'; if the stronger continuing invariant is intended, revalidate every kept backup during cleanup.
